_meta.description: Hand-verified facts for the exams seeded by database_setup.py. Every record carries the official source it was checked against. Values that could not be confirmed against an official or authoritative source are the string 'Information not available' rather than a guess.
_meta.verification_policy: Prefer the conducting body's own notification or careers page. Cutoffs are only recorded when the conducting body publishes them officially.
_meta.caveat: Eligibility rules, vacancy counts and pay change with every notification cycle. Always re-check the official_website before relying on a row.

exams.nationality: For IAS and IPS: must be a citizen of India. For other services: citizen of India, or subject of Nepal or Bhutan, or a Tibetan refugee who came to India before 1 January 1962, or a person of Indian origin who migrated from specified countries with intent to settle permanently in India.
exams.age_limits: 21 to 32 years for the unreserved category, reckoned as on 1 August of the examination year.
exams.age_relax: OBC (non-creamy layer): 3 years (to 35). SC/ST: 5 years (to 37). PwBD: 10 years (General/EWS to 42, OBC to 45, SC/ST to 47). Defence personnel disabled in operations and ex-servicemen: up to 5 years as per the notification.
exams.edu_qual: A bachelor's degree in any discipline from a recognised university. No minimum percentage is prescribed. Final-year students may apply provisionally and must produce proof of passing before the Main examination.
exams.attempts: General/EWS: 6. OBC: 9. SC/ST: unlimited up to the upper age limit. PwBD: 9 for General/EWS/OBC and unlimited for SC/ST. Appearing in any one Prelims paper counts as an attempt.
exams.physical_std: No physical efficiency test for the written stages. Service-specific medical and physical standards apply after selection, and are strictest for the IPS.
exams.stages: Three stages: Preliminary (objective, screening only), Main (written, descriptive) and Personality Test (interview).
exams.num_papers: Prelims: 2 papers. Main: 9 papers, of which 7 count towards merit and 2 (one Indian language and English) are qualifying.
exams.q_type: Prelims: multiple choice. Main: conventional essay/descriptive answers.
exams.duration: Each Prelims paper is 2 hours. Each Main paper is 3 hours.
exams.marking_scheme: Prelims: Paper I is 200 marks and Paper II (CSAT) is 200 marks and is qualifying at 33 percent. One third of the marks assigned to a question is deducted for each wrong answer. Main: 1750 marks counted for merit plus 275 marks for the Personality Test, giving a final total of 2025.

exams.nationality: A citizen of India, or a subject of Nepal or Bhutan, or a Tibetan refugee who came to India before 1 January 1962, or a person of Indian origin who migrated from specified countries with intent to settle permanently in India.
exams.age_limits: 21 to 30 years for Officers in Grade B (Direct Recruit) - General, reckoned as on the date given in the notification.
exams.age_relax: OBC: 3 years. SC/ST: 5 years. PwBD: 10 years for General/EWS, 13 years for OBC and 15 years for SC/ST. Candidates holding an M.Phil may apply up to 32 and a Ph.D. up to 34. Ex-servicemen and existing RBI staff get relaxation as per the notification.
exams.edu_qual: Grade B General: a bachelor's degree in any discipline with at least 60 percent marks (50 percent for SC/ST/PwBD), or a postgraduate degree with at least 55 percent marks in aggregate of all semesters. Candidates who have passed the final examination of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India may also apply. DEPR and DSIM streams require a specified master's degree in economics or statistics respectively.
exams.attempts: Six attempts for General category candidates. No attempt limit for SC, ST, OBC and PwBD candidates.
exams.physical_std: No physical efficiency test. Candidates must be medically fit as certified by the Bank.
exams.stages: Three stages: Phase I (online objective screening), Phase II (online, objective plus descriptive) and Interview.
exams.num_papers: Phase I: one composite objective paper. Phase II: three papers for the General stream (Economic and Social Issues, English Writing Skills, and Finance and Management).
exams.q_type: Phase I: multiple choice. Phase II: a mix of multiple choice and descriptive answers typed online.
exams.duration: Phase I: 120 minutes. Phase II: 30 to 90 minutes per paper depending on the paper.
exams.marking_scheme: Negative marking of one fourth of the marks assigned applies to wrong answers in the objective papers. Phase I is screening only and its marks do not count towards the final merit.

exams.nationality: A citizen of India, or a subject of Nepal or Bhutan, or a Tibetan refugee who came to India before 1 January 1962, or a person of Indian origin who migrated from specified countries with intent to settle permanently in India.
exams.age_limits: 21 to 30 years, reckoned as on the cut-off date stated in the advertisement (1 April 2025 in the 2025-26 cycle).
exams.age_relax: SC/ST: 5 years. OBC (non-creamy layer): 3 years. PwBD: 10 years for General, 13 for OBC and 15 for SC/ST. Ex-servicemen and candidates domiciled in Jammu and Kashmir during the specified period get relaxation as per the advertisement.
exams.edu_qual: A graduate degree in any discipline from a recognised university, or an equivalent qualification recognised by the central government. Final-year students may apply provisionally and must produce proof of graduation by the date stated in the advertisement. Integrated dual degree, medical, engineering, chartered accountancy and cost accountancy holders are eligible.
exams.attempts: General/EWS: 4. OBC: 7. SC/ST: no limit. PwBD candidates get the relaxed limit for their category. Appearing in the Preliminary examination is not counted; appearing in the Main examination counts as one attempt.
exams.physical_std: No physical efficiency test. Candidates must be medically fit.
exams.stages: Three stages: Preliminary examination, Main examination, and a Psychometric test followed by Group Exercise and Interview.
exams.num_papers: Preliminary: one composite objective paper. Main: one objective paper of four sections plus a descriptive English test.
exams.q_type: Objective multiple choice, plus a descriptive letter and essay in the Main examination.
exams.duration: Preliminary: 60 minutes. Main: 3 hours objective plus 30 minutes descriptive.
exams.marking_scheme: Preliminary: 100 marks, qualifying only. Main: 200 marks objective plus 50 marks descriptive. One fourth of the marks assigned to a question is deducted for a wrong answer. Final merit is based on the Main examination and the interview stage.

exams.nationality: A citizen of India, or a subject of Nepal or Bhutan, or a Tibetan refugee who came to India before 1 January 1962, or a person of Indian origin who migrated from specified countries with intent to settle permanently in India.
exams.age_limits: 20 to 30 years, reckoned as on the cut-off date stated in the notification.
exams.age_relax: SC/ST: 5 years. OBC (non-creamy layer): 3 years. PwBD: 10 years. Ex-servicemen and commissioned officers including ECOs and SSCOs with at least five years of military service: 5 years.
exams.edu_qual: A degree in any discipline from a university recognised by the Government of India, or an equivalent qualification recognised as such by the central government. No minimum percentage is prescribed. Computer literacy is required.
exams.attempts: No limit on the number of attempts within the prescribed age limit.
exams.physical_std: No physical efficiency test. Candidates must be medically fit.
exams.stages: Three stages: Preliminary examination, Main examination and Interview conducted by the participating banks.
exams.num_papers: Preliminary: one composite objective paper of three sections. Main: one objective paper of four sections plus a descriptive English paper.
exams.q_type: Objective multiple choice, plus a descriptive letter and essay in the Main examination.
exams.duration: Preliminary: 60 minutes. Main: 3 hours objective plus 30 minutes descriptive.
exams.marking_scheme: Preliminary: 100 marks, qualifying only. Main: 200 marks objective plus 25 marks descriptive. One fourth of the marks assigned to a question is deducted for a wrong answer. Final merit combines the Main examination (80 percent weight) and the interview (20 percent weight).

exams.nationality: A citizen of India, or a subject of Nepal or Bhutan, or a Tibetan refugee who came to India before 1 January 1962, or a person of Indian origin who migrated from specified countries with intent to settle permanently in India.
exams.age_limits: Varies by post. For Assistant Audit Officer and Assistant Accounts Officer under the C&AG the limit is 18 to 30 years, reckoned as on the cut-off date in the notification. Other CGL posts use 18 to 27, 18 to 30 or 20 to 30 depending on the post.
exams.age_relax: OBC: 3 years. SC/ST: 5 years. PwBD (unreserved): 10 years. PwBD (OBC): 13 years. PwBD (SC/ST): 15 years. Ex-servicemen: 3 years after deducting military service rendered. Further relaxations apply to specified categories per the notification.
exams.edu_qual: A bachelor's degree in any discipline from a recognised university for most posts. Assistant Audit Officer and Assistant Accounts Officer list Chartered Accountant, Cost and Management Accountant, Company Secretary or a master's in Commerce or Business Studies as desirable. Junior Statistical Officer requires a degree with Mathematics or Statistics as specified in the notification.
exams.attempts: No limit on the number of attempts within the prescribed age limit.
exams.physical_std: Not required for Assistant Audit Officer. Physical standards and a physical efficiency test apply only to specific posts such as Inspector in the Central Bureau of Narcotics and Sub-Inspector posts.
exams.stages: Two computer-based tiers followed by document verification. A Data Entry Speed Test or Computer Proficiency Test applies to certain posts.
exams.num_papers: Tier I: one paper. Tier II: Paper I is compulsory for all candidates; Paper II applies to Junior Statistical Officer and Statistical Investigator candidates; Paper III (Finance and Economics) applies to Assistant Audit Officer and Assistant Accounts Officer candidates.
exams.q_type: Objective multiple choice, delivered as a computer-based test.
exams.duration: Tier I: 60 minutes. Tier II Paper I: 2 hours 15 minutes across its sessions, plus the skill tests where applicable.
exams.marking_scheme: Tier I: 200 marks with 0.50 deducted per wrong answer. Tier II: negative marking of 1 mark per wrong answer in Section III and 0.50 in other sections, as specified in the notification. Final merit is based on Tier II.

exams.nationality: An unmarried candidate who is a citizen of India, or a subject of Nepal, or a Tibetan refugee who came to India before 1 January 1962, or a person of Indian origin who migrated from specified countries with intent to settle permanently in India.
exams.age_limits: Approximately 16.5 to 19.5 years. The notification states the exact date-of-birth window for each cycle rather than an age in years.
exams.age_relax: No age relaxation is given for any category. The date-of-birth window in the notification is absolute.
exams.edu_qual: Army wing: passed or appearing in the 12th class of the 10+2 pattern. Air Force, Naval wings and the 10+2 Cadet Entry Scheme at the Indian Naval Academy: 12th class with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics.
exams.attempts: No limit on the number of attempts, but the narrow date-of-birth window in practice permits about three.
exams.physical_std: Candidates must be physically fit per the detailed standards in the notification, covering minimum height, weight for height, chest expansion, vision and dental fitness. Standards differ by service and a full medical board follows the SSB interview.
exams.stages: Two stages: a written examination followed by the Services Selection Board interview, which itself runs over about five days and includes screening, psychological tests, group testing and a personal interview.
exams.num_papers: Two papers: Mathematics, and General Ability Test.
exams.duration: 2 hours 30 minutes for each of the two papers.
exams.marking_scheme: Mathematics: 300 marks. General Ability Test: 600 marks. Written total 900 marks, with the SSB interview carrying a further 900 marks. One third of the marks assigned to a question is deducted for a wrong answer.

exams.conducting_body: Indian Space Research Organisation - Centralised Recruitment Board
exams.nationality: Must be a citizen of India.
exams.age_limits: Upper age limit of 28 years for Scientist/Engineer SC recruited on the basis of BE/B.Tech or a GATE score. The limit is 30 years for entry based on ME/M.Tech or an engineering degree with an MBA.
exams.age_relax: OBC: 3 years. SC/ST: 5 years. Ex-servicemen and persons with benchmark disabilities: as per Government of India orders. Serving central government employees: as per rules.
exams.edu_qual: BE/B.Tech or equivalent in the relevant discipline with an aggregate of at least 65 percent marks or CGPA 6.84 on a 10-point scale. The qualification must have been completed within the duration prescribed by the university. ME/M.Tech entry requires at least 60 percent or CGPA 6.5 with the BE/B.Tech pre-eligibility above.
exams.attempts: No limit on the number of attempts within the prescribed age limit.
exams.physical_std: No physical efficiency test. Appointment is subject to a medical fitness certificate.
exams.stages: For written-test based recruitment: a written test followed by an interview. For GATE-score based recruitment: shortlisting on the GATE score followed by an interview only.
exams.num_papers: One written paper of 100 questions, in two parts.
exams.q_type: Objective multiple choice. Part A covers the discipline-specific area with 80 questions; Part B is an aptitude and ability test.
exams.duration: As stated in the call letter for each recruitment cycle; typically 90 to 120 minutes.
exams.marking_scheme: Part A carries 1 mark per question with one third of a mark deducted for a wrong answer. Where both a written test and an interview are held, each carries 50 percent weight in the final merit list.

exams.conducting_body: Defence Research and Development Organisation - Recruitment and Assessment Centre
exams.nationality: Must be a citizen of India.
exams.age_limits: Upper age limit of 35 years for Scientist B under the GATE-based advertisement, reckoned as on the closing date of the application.
exams.age_relax: OBC (non-creamy layer): 3 years. SC/ST: 5 years. Persons with benchmark disabilities: 10 years. Central government civilian employees in allied posts: 5 years. Ex-servicemen: as per rules.
exams.edu_qual: At least a first-class bachelor's degree in the relevant engineering discipline, or a first-class master's degree in the relevant science discipline, together with a valid GATE score in the notified paper code.
exams.attempts: No limit on the number of attempts within the prescribed age limit.
exams.physical_std: No physical efficiency test. Appointment is subject to medical fitness and security clearance.
exams.stages: Two stages: shortlisting on the basis of the GATE score, followed by a personal interview. DRDO also runs a separate written entry test in cycles where GATE is not used.
exams.num_papers: Not applicable for the GATE-based route; the GATE paper itself serves as the written stage.
exams.q_type: Not applicable for the GATE-based route. Personal interview assesses technical depth.
exams.duration: Not applicable for the GATE-based route.
exams.marking_scheme: Final selection under the GATE-based route weighs the GATE score at 80 percent and the personal interview at 20 percent. Shortlisting for interview is typically in a 1:10 ratio, discipline-wise and category-wise.

exams.nationality: A citizen of India, or a subject of Nepal or Bhutan, or a Tibetan refugee who came to India before 1 January 1962, or a person of Indian origin who migrated from specified countries with intent to settle permanently in India. Certain services are restricted to Indian citizens.
exams.age_limits: 21 to 30 years for the unreserved category, reckoned as on 1 January of the examination year.
exams.age_relax: OBC: 3 years (to 33). SC/ST: 5 years (to 35). Ex-servicemen: 5 years. Persons with benchmark disabilities: 10 years. Candidates domiciled in Jammu and Kashmir during the specified period and certain defence personnel get relaxation as per the notification.
exams.edu_qual: A degree in engineering from a recognised university, or having passed Sections A and B of the Institution Examinations of the Institution of Engineers (India), or an equivalent qualification listed in the notification. Wireless Communication, Electronics, Radio Physics or Radio Engineering degrees are accepted for specific streams.
exams.attempts: No limit on the number of attempts within the prescribed age limit.
exams.physical_std: Candidates must meet the physical standards laid down in the notification, which vary by service. A medical examination follows the written stages.
exams.stages: Three stages: Preliminary (objective), Main (conventional) and Personality Test.
exams.num_papers: Preliminary: 2 papers (General Studies and Engineering Aptitude, and the discipline-specific paper). Main: 2 conventional papers in the discipline.
exams.q_type: Preliminary: objective multiple choice. Main: conventional descriptive answers.
exams.duration: Preliminary Paper I: 2 hours. Preliminary Paper II: 3 hours. Each Main paper: 3 hours.
exams.marking_scheme: Preliminary: 200 plus 300 marks. Main: 300 plus 300 marks. Personality Test: 200 marks. Overall total 1300 marks. One third of the marks assigned is deducted for each wrong answer in the objective papers.

exams.nationality: Must be a citizen of India.
exams.age_limits: 21 to 30 years for AAO Generalist, reckoned as on the cut-off date in the notification (1 August 2025 in the 2025 cycle). AAO Legal and AAO Chartered Accountant use 21 to 32 years.
exams.age_relax: SC/ST: 5 years. OBC (non-creamy layer): 3 years. Persons with benchmark disabilities: 10 years. Confirmed LIC employees and ex-servicemen get relaxation as per the notification.
exams.edu_qual: AAO Generalist: a bachelor's degree in any discipline from a recognised Indian university or institution. Specialist streams require the corresponding professional qualification, such as a law degree for AAO Legal, membership of the ICAI for AAO Chartered Accountant, or actuarial papers for AAO Actuarial.
exams.attempts: No limit on the number of attempts within the prescribed age limit.
exams.physical_std: No physical efficiency test. Appointment is subject to a pre-recruitment medical examination.
exams.stages: Three stages: Preliminary examination, Main examination and Interview, followed by a pre-recruitment medical examination.
exams.num_papers: Preliminary: one composite objective paper of three sections. Main: one objective paper plus a descriptive English test.
exams.q_type: Objective multiple choice, plus a descriptive English paper in the Main examination.
exams.duration: Preliminary: 60 minutes. Main: 120 minutes objective plus 30 minutes descriptive.
exams.marking_scheme: Preliminary: 100 marks, qualifying only. Main: 300 marks objective plus 25 marks descriptive. Penalty for wrong answers is as stated in the notification for the cycle.
